sentences.text:
--------
Chhatru Kumar Mahto, aged about 30 years, son of Shri Janki Mahto, resident of Village-Jamhar,
P.O. & P.S.-Kasmar, District-Bokaro ... ... Appellant Versus The State of Jharkhand ...... Respondent

-----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr.Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'Ble Mr. Justice
Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
--------
For the Appellant : Mr. Vikas Kumar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Manoj Kr. Mishra, A.P.P.
--------

Order No. 04/ Dated: 22nd December, 2025 I.A. No. 15895 of 2025 Heard Mr. Vikas Kumar,
learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. appearing for the State.
2.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.
3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 498A & 304B of I.P.C. and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years.
4. It has been alleged that the daughter of the informant died in unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial house.

5. Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that there are variation in the evidence of the witnesses with respect to the exact amount which was purportedly demanded by the appellant and the days on which such demands were made.

6. Learned counsel submits that though in the written report mention has been made about a demand of Rs. 2,00,000/- through Whatsapp but the investigating officer failed to inquire as to Chhatru Kumar Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144267768/
1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: whether indeed any such message was sent by the appellant or not.
Learned counsel adds that the appellant is in custody for four years and four months.
7. Learned A.P.P. appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

8. It appears that the deceased had died within 14 months of her marriage with the appellant and just prior to her death there was a demand of dowry as would be evident from the testimony of the witnesses.
The cause of death has been opined to be on account of asphyxia due to hanging.
9. On such consideration, therefore we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail and the prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected, at this stage.
10. The aforesaid I.A. stands disposed of.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.)
